blockers:
- V1 (validated, introduced by this range): the force-push deny rule in /home/davidbasile/dev/holyagent-fix-cli-and-vcs/packages/runtime/src/cli/shell.ts (`forces`, line 239) is a narrow allow-list. The previous hook denied every `git push`, and now plain pushes pass. `git push --mirror <remote>` force-updates and deletes remote refs and passes: no `--force`, no `-f` cluster, no `+` refspec. `git push $'\x2d\x2dforce' origin main` also passes. `scanAnsiC` (lines 86-98) does not decode hex, octal or unicode escapes, so the word becomes `x2dx2dforce`, while bash passes `--force` to git. Git also accepts unambiguous abbreviations such as `--force-with` or `--force-w`, which fail both the `=== "--force"` and `startsWith("--force-with-lease")` tests. Precondition: the model, for example after prompt injection, picks one of these spellings. The `if` rule `Bash(*git*push*)` matches all of them, so the hook runs and finds no write. Impact: published history is rewritten with no deny and no user approval, which the REDIRECTS text promises is blocked. Fix: deny on the unknown instead of allowing it. For `git push`, deny any word that is not a known-safe literal, or any word containing `$`, `{`, `*` or a leftover escape. Add `--mirror`, `--delete` and `--prune` to the list, and match long options by prefix.
- V2 (validated by tracing the scanner; the `<<` heredoc code predates the range, but this range's deny rules depend on it): the here-string `<<<` is read as a heredoc, so a following line is never scanned. `scanCode` shell.ts:152 skips a `<<` only when the next character is `<`. At the first `<` of `<<<` that holds, so it falls through to the redirect branch at line 170. At the second `<`, `next` is `<` and `text[index+2]` is a space, so `readHeredoc` runs. Input: `cat <<< x\ngit commit -m y`, or `: <<< x\ngit push --force`. `readHeredoc` records the delimiter `x`. At the newline, `skipHeredocs` (lines 24-33) discards every later line until one equals `x`, which never comes, so the rest of the command is dropped. Bash runs the here-string and the next line normally. `gitWrites` returns `[]`, so the hook says nothing and the commit or force push goes ahead. `$((1<<2))` followed by a newline has the same effect. Precondition: a multi-line Bash command containing `git`, `commit` or `push` in order, which is an ordinary shape. The tests (`shell.test.ts`) have no `<<<` or `$((…<<…))` case. Fix: treat `<<<` as a redirect operator whose target word is read as a word, and open a heredoc only for exactly `<<` or `<<-`.
notes:
- Scope and limits: the built-in /security-review loaded as the genuine built-in text. It diffed the main checkout against origin/HEAD, which is clean, so it covered none of the PR6 range. I reviewed bf31fac..841ef47 by reading pr6-review.diff and the files in the holyagent-fix-cli-and-vcs worktree. The role has no shell, so I ran no code, tests or live exploit, and every finding is from reading the code and tracing it by hand. The tree may have been moving, since other workers share it.
- V3 (validated, hook gap; the hook comment already admits variables, aliases and scripts): more ways to hide a commit or force push from `gitWrites` while the `if` rule still matches. (a) Nested backticks: ``echo `echo \`git commit -m x\```. The scanner treats the escaped backtick as a literal character, producing words like `` `git ``, and never sees `git commit`. (b) Wrappers missing from `WRAPPERS`: `setsid`, `stdbuf`, `ionice`, `flock`, `watch`, `find -exec`, `parallel`, `ssh`, `su -c`, `script -c`, and `env -S 'git commit'`, whose value is skipped as a valued option. Also `fish -c`, which is not in `SHELLS`. (c) A shell reading its script from stdin, a heredoc or a pipe: `bash <<'EOF'\ngit commit -m x\nEOF`, `echo 'git commit -m x' | sh`, `eval 'git commit -m x'`. `writesOf` only follows `sh -c <literal>`. (d) Git global options that take their value as the next word but are missing from `VALUE_OPTIONS` (`--attr-source <tree>`, `--config-env <name=env>`): `git --attr-source HEAD commit -m x` makes the subcommand look like `HEAD`. (e) Inline aliases: `git -c alias.ci=commit ci -m x`. (f) Brace expansion: `git comm{it,it} -m 'commit'`. (g) Hex escapes in the subcommand, such as `$'\x63ommit'`. The `if` rule only needs literal `git` followed later by literal `commit` text, so any of these plus a mention in a message satisfies it. The comment in hook.ts line 649 and the docs say wrappers, `sh -c`, `xargs` and subshells that show the words are denied. That overstates the coverage for the unlisted wrappers in (b) and (c). Suggested fix: when the `if` rule matches and the scanner finds no write, deny any command that has a `git` word followed by `commit` or `push` within a non-literal construct, or fall back to `permissionDecision: "ask"` rather than silence.
- V4 (validated by reading, adversarial input needed): the hook fails open on a parse failure. `vcs-redirect` wraps `gitWrites` in `Effect.try`, then `Effect.orElseSucceed(() => NOTHING)` (hook.ts 721-731), so any exception becomes silence even though the hook sets `onFailure: block`. `scanCode` recurses once per `$(` or backtick, and `writesOf` recurses per `sh -c`, with no depth cap. A command of tens of thousands of nested `$(` followed by `git commit` can overflow the JS stack. The RangeError is caught and the call is allowed. The only test is a 3000-round random fuzz of short strings, which cannot reach that depth. Fix: cap the depth in the scanner, and on any exception or cap return a deny or ask, not NOTHING. A deny cannot stop a call that has no git write, because the `if` rule has already matched the words.
- S1 (suspicion, needs a probe against Claude Code): `if: Bash(*git*commit*)` and `Bash(*git*push*)` may not match multi-line commands, such as `echo hi\ngit commit -m x` or `git \\\n commit`, if the glob compiles `*` to `.*` without the dotAll flag. The probe described in generate.ts covered `&&` lists and subshells, not newlines. If a newline breaks the match, the hook never runs for those commands. I could not run Claude Code to check.
- V5 (validated, low): the `commit-msg` hook (hook.ts 746-762) drops lines starting with `#` before the forbidden-phrase check. `git commit -m $'fix\n# the user asked'` keeps the `#` lines in the message, because the default cleanup for `-m` is `whitespace`, not `strip`, so the phrase check is skipped. `vcs commit` itself checks the full text, so only hand-made commits are affected. The file path comes from git as argv and is trusted. The hook fails closed when settings cannot be read. `.holyagent/config.json` `vcs.allowWords` is editable by the agent and can weaken the check; this is by design and low risk.
- V6 (low, policy not security): `requireOwnIdentity` (commit.ts 40-47) reads `git config user.name` and `user.email`. Git's real identity can be overridden by GIT_AUTHOR_*, GIT_COMMITTER_* and EMAIL, so the check can disagree with the commit author. Environment is trusted per the review precedents, so I do not count this. `looksLikeAgent` only matches `noreply@anthropic.com` or a name starting with `claude`.
- V7 (low): `stagedPaths` in commit.ts uses `git diff --cached --name-only` without `--relative`, so paths are repo-root-relative, while the scope is relative to the project root. If the project is a subdirectory of the git repository, an unrelated staged file at the same relative prefix could count as in scope and be committed. In the usual case the project root is the repository root and this does not apply. I did not confirm how `call.directory` and the git cwd relate.
- Plain `git push` is now allowed by design. Other commit-creating commands (`commit-tree`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`, `merge`, `am`) are not covered by the redirect. The repository's commit-msg hook covers some of them, but only where it is installed and `--no-verify` or `core.hooksPath` is not set. A forced push can also be configured with a `+` refspec in `remote.*.push`, which the deny rule does not see.
- Findings sound: (1) `vcs commit`: Bun Shell `$` spreads array arguments as separate escaped words (process.ts). The message goes to `git commit -m <headline> [-m <body>]`, so a leading dash is only a value. Paths pass `pathProblem` and `git --literal-pathspecs … -- paths`, so there is no magic pathspec or option injection. The staged-outside-scope check refuses a wider commit. (2) `vcs pr`: `readBodyFile` is solid. It rejects `.git` segments, resolves symlinks and enforces containment, opens with O_NOFOLLOW, checks size and regular file on the descriptor, re-resolves the path afterwards, and honors `git check-ignore`. The repo slug must match `[\w.-]+/[\w.-]+`. `--update` must match `^[1-9]\d*$` and goes through `apiPath`. The branch passes `validBranch`. The payload goes to gh on stdin as JSON, so no argument injection. (3) The lefthook `{1}` message-file path comes from git. (4) A payload decode failure in `vcs-redirect` exits 1, and `onFailure: block` then blocks. (5) No new dependencies or secret handling in the reviewed files.
